content: 1. Over the past week, how frequently did the child’s father engage in play activities to help the child learn new things? 1: Did not play at all. 2: Played on a few days of the week but not every day. 3: Played one or two times every day. 4: Played more than two times every day. 2. Over the past week, how frequently did other family members engage in play activities to help the child learn new things? 1: Did not play at all. 2: Played on a few days of the week but not every day. 3: Played one or two times every day. 4: Played more than two times every day. 3. Have you been shown this card at the clinic or by a health worker, or have you received any recommendations on how to play and communicate with your child? (Show card) 1: Yes. 2: No. 4. If the answer is No, proceed to Question 83. If Yes, which of the following recommendations have you heard? (Read recommendations for the child’s age group and the next younger age group.) Heard? (1 = Yes; 2 = No) Have you tried this at home? (1 = Yes; 2 = No) For children aged 0–6 months: Provide large, bright objects for the child to reach for. Look into the child’s eyes and smile. Practice exclusive breastfeeding. For children aged 6–12 months: Offer clean and safe household items for the child to handle, bang, and drop. Respond to the child’s sounds and interests; name objects for the child. Introduce complementary feeding with appropriate quantity and quality of food. For children aged 12–24 months: Provide objects of different sizes for stacking or placing into and removing from containers. Ask the child simple questions or respond to their attempts to communicate. Encourage eating family foods, increasing food variety, and providing vitamins. Support the child in learning to eat independently, such as holding a spoon. For children aged 24 months and above: Help the child count, name, and compare objects or create simple toys. Encourage the child to talk and answer their questions. 5. I will now provide a list of individuals or groups you might have discussed your child’s development with. For each, please indicate how often you have spoken to them about your child’s development: Child’s father: 1: Not at all. 2: A few times a month. 3: A few times a week. 4: Every day. Mother-in-law: Same response options as above. Other family members or friends: Same response options as above. Doctor, nurse, or other health worker: Same response options as above. Teacher: Same response options as above. Religious or community leader: Same response options as above. Community health promoter or women’s group: Same response options as above. 6. How often have you read articles from newspapers, magazines, or books about your child’s learning, thinking, or emotional development in the last month? 1: Not at all. 2: A few times a month. 3: A few times a week. 4: Every day. 7. How many television programs have you watched about your child’s learning, thinking, or emotional development in the last month? 1: Not at all. 2: A few times a month. 3: A few times a week. 4: Every day. 8. What do you think is the most reliable source of information? 1: Family. 2: TV and media. 3: Health workers. 4: Teachers. 5: Other. 9. How would you most like to receive this information? 1: From a health worker. 2: From others in the health center. 3: Through distributed materials. 4: Via TV and radio. 5: I do not need or want more information. 10. If you want more information, what would you like to know? 11. How many providers in your country have received training in Care for Child Development (CCD)? 12. How many providers have you evaluated using the E&M Package? 13. Based on your evaluation, approximately what percentage of trained providers are implementing the intervention, and what percentage of their clients are being reached? 14. What is the most commonly used component of the intervention? a) Asking caregivers what they are doing to stimulate their child. b) Counseling caregivers on how to stimulate their child’s development. c) Demonstrating homemade toys to caregivers. d) Asking about barriers preventing caregivers from using CCD. e) Helping caregivers find solutions to these barriers. 15. What is the least commonly used component of the intervention? (Same options as above.) 16. In your opinion, do most providers who have received CCD training value this intervention as a core component of their practice? a) Yes. b) No. 17. What are the major barriers preventing the use of CCD? a) Insufficient training. b) Lack of supervision, feedback, or reinforcement. c) Providers do not value CCD. d) Insufficient time allocated per child visit. e) Other (please describe). 18. What plans have been developed to overcome these barriers? a) Designating a person to provide supervision and support. b) Assigning a ‘champion’ to lead implementation efforts. c) Scheduling regular group feedback and support meetings. d) Other (please explain). 19. How will CCD be used in your country over the next three years? Include the number of providers to be trained, their backgrounds, and the number of children and caregivers to be counseled. 20. What support would you like to receive from WHO/UNICEF regarding CCD implementation in your country? 21. In which system is CCD being implemented? a) Health-care system. b) Education system. c) Social services system. d) Non-governmental organization. e) Academic institution. f) Other (please explain). 22. Please list the positive changes observed in communities as a result of CCD, providing examples. 23. What key factors have contributed to these positive changes in communities? 24. Please list changes in the system where CCD is being implemented, providing examples. 25. What key factors have contributed to these changes in the system? 26. What other positive changes do you expect in communities over the next two years? 27. What other positive changes do you expect in the systems over the next two years? 28. What was the date of the training? 29. How were the CCD providers trained? a) Using the standard WHO/CDI training package and materials. b) Modified WHO/CDI training (please describe). 30. Did the training include clinical practice for the trainees? 31. Who were the trainers? (Provide the number and their affiliations.) 32. How many providers were trained, and what were their backgrounds? 33. What is your age? 34. What is your gender? a) Female. b) Male. 35. What is your occupation? (Circle one.) a) Nurse. b) General physician/medical doctor. c) Pediatrician. d) Home health visitor. e) Home visitor (other). f) Child development specialist. g) Psychologist. h) Educator/teacher. i) Social worker. j) Paraprofessional (no specific background). k) Other (please specify). 36. What is the date and location of the CCD training? 37. How many children aged 0–3 years do you provide services for per day? 38. How many home visits do you conduct per month? 39. Have you received any training related to child development other than CCD? a) No. b) Yes (please specify). 40. How do you currently use CCD in practice? a) I do not remember CCD. b) I remember CCD but have not had the chance to use it (please explain why). c) I use CCD with very few children-caregivers (less than ¼). d) I use CCD with some children-caregivers (¼–½). e) I use CCD with many children-caregivers (½–¾). f) I use CCD with most children-caregivers (more than ¾). g) Other (please explain). 41. If you are not using CCD with all your clients, please indicate the reasons: a) It takes too long to use CCD. b) I see too many children and families and lack time. c) The training was inadequate. d) CCD intervention is not user-friendly. e) Training materials are inadequate. f) Caregivers are not interested in learning CCD messages. g) I do not prioritize CCD. h) I do not receive monetary compensation for using CCD. i) I do not receive supervision or feedback. j) I have lost motivation to use CCD. k) There is no system to evaluate and report CCD outcomes. l) Other barriers (please specify). 42. Is there a system in place for receiving supervision or feedback for CCD? a) No. b) Yes (please specify frequency and provider of supervision/feedback). 43. If you are using CCD with some clients, what factors facilitate its use? a) Home visits. b) Well-child care visits. c) Sufficient time with clients. d) Following the same family over time. e) Other (please explain).
